# WordFormat

> Automated paper formatting tool

## Project Introduction

**WordFormat** is an automated Word document format checking and correction tool developed in Python, designed specifically for format compliance review of academic papers (undergraduate, master's, and doctoral theses, journal papers, etc.). The tool can intelligently parse Word document structure, identify paragraph types such as headings, abstracts, body text, and references, automatically validate document formatting against custom formatting rules, and add comments at non-compliant locations or directly fix formatting issues, greatly improving the efficiency of paper format review.

## Features

### Core Capabilities
- **Intelligent document structure parsing**: Based on an ONNX model, automatically identifies paragraph types such as headings, abstracts, body text, keywords, and references, generating structured JSON configuration files
- **Structural short-circuit recognition**: Image paragraphs, formula paragraphs (OMML, including standalone formula numbers such as （2-1）), and tables are determined directly from the XML structure without relying on model confidence; formula paragraphs can also be centered according to configuration
- **Fine-grained format validation**: Supports full-dimension checks for paragraph formatting (alignment, line spacing, indentation, paragraph spacing) and character formatting (font, font size, color, bold/italic/underline)
- **Multi-level heading management**: Accurately identifies level 1/2/3 headings and supports validation against custom heading format specifications
- **Multilingual adaptation**: Distinguishes Chinese and English font and format rules, fully supporting format checks for mixed Chinese-English documents
- **Flexible interaction**: Supports a step-by-step workflow of "generate structure file → manually adjust → run validation," balancing automation and flexibility

### Practical Features
- **Markdown to Word**: Converts Markdown files directly into formatted .docx documents, preserving heading hierarchy and automatically applying the formatting specifications from the configuration
- **Automatic comment generation**: Automatically adds Word comments at format violation locations, annotating issue types and correction suggestions
- **Document structure visualization**: The `wordf tree` command displays document paragraph classification and hierarchy as a tree, with support for filtering by category and displaying confidence scores
- **One-click format fixing**: Supports automatic correction of some common formatting issues according to specifications (e.g., heading font sizes, body line spacing)
- **Automatic heading numbering**: Supports clearing manual numbering and applying Word automatic numbering, with customizable numbering templates (e.g., "Chapter X", "1.1.1"), numbering suffixes (tab, space, or none), and indentation settings
- **Headers, footers, and page setup**: Validates font size, font, alignment, and missing content section by section; fixes can insert PAGE page-number fields, and write page margins, paper size and orientation, starting page number and page-number format, different first page, different odd and even pages, and update fields on open
- **Web visualization interface**: Built-in Vue frontend; launch the graphical control panel with one command via `wordf startapi`, no command line needed
- **Custom configuration**: Flexibly define format specifications through YAML configuration files, adapting to the formatting requirements of different schools and journals

> **"Though still clumsy for now, Yuki will grow slowly. So... don't you dare leave me behind!"**

Yuki is a personal intelligent assistant system built on a Python asynchronous architecture. It interacts with its owner and group chats through the QQ platform (NapCat framework). Yuki uses the Function Call tool `delegate_to_maid`, through which Yuki can hand complex tasks to a background "little maid" for processing.

# SangTacReader — Unofficial iOS client for sangtacviet

Wraps the sangtacviet web version in a native iOS shell: a Capacitor 8 app that remotely loads `sangtacviet.com/app.v2.php` and supplies the native capabilities the site's frontend depends on, so the site runs in "app mode". - Book list / search / latest updates / rankings, novel details, follow / bookmarks / likes
- Chapter list and body reading (left-right paging by default, can switch to scrolling)
- Native TTS reading, starting from the line visible on screen
- Offline download: resumable, downloaded chapters skipped automatically, can pause / resume / delete
- Export to TXT / EPUB (with cover and title), via the system share sheet
- Comment and community post translation: system offline translation first, or bring your own API key
- Interface localized to Chinese (Vietnamese → Simplified Chinese); on first launch it follows the iOS system language, which can be changed later in settings

- Reader safe-area adaptation (Dynamic Island / Home Indicator), long-press menu, keyboard popup positioning

After pushing to `main`, GitHub Actions automatically builds an **unsigned** IPA and refreshes the same rolling Release:

```
https://github.com/IamNewHands/SangTacReader/releases/latest/download/SangTacReader-unsigned.ipa
```

The site frontend decides whether to use "app mode" (native network stack) or "web mode" (web XHR, which is prone to hitting Cloudflare) based on whether `window.Capacitor` exists. Say “做签到任务” (“do check-in tasks”), “红包签到” (“red-packet check-in”), or “赚元宝” (“earn Yuanbao”) to trigger the check-in module. # CS2 Coach Agent

**From match recordings to traceable event analysis, player profiles, and training recommendations**

CS2 Coach Agent is an engineering project for CS2 match review: it parses real `.dem` recordings, links round events with historical retrieval evidence, generates verifiable match reports, and supports player comparison, source drill-down, and read-only follow-up questions after saving.

The system uses LangGraph to orchestrate analysis nodes. Metrics, report facts, and citations are generated by code; the model selects training themes within a whitelist. The project focuses on the complete data pipeline, explainable retrieval boundaries, fault handling, and reproducible evaluation.

## Reading guide

- Understand the product: [What it can do](#能做什么) · [Player profiles and relation queries](#选手画像与关系查询)
- Understand the implementation: [Architecture and design trade-offs](#架构与设计取舍) · [Project structure and further reading](#项目结构与进一步阅读)

- Verification results: [Current validation results](#当前验证结果) · [Tests and benchmarks](#测试与-benchmark) · [Known limitations](#已知边界)

## Why this project

A plausible-sounding review is not necessarily supported by match evidence: the kill count may use the wrong participant denominator, retrieval results may mention only two players without the specified interaction occurring, and training advice may write event correlations as tactical causes. This project breaks these problems down into inspectable inputs, statistics, retrieval, and output contracts.

For users, the goal is to find rounds worth reviewing from a recording and understand the basis for conclusions. gybeyond1/Veyra.body:
# Veyra

Veyra is a **short-drama aggregator player**: an Android client (APK) plus a self-hosted Node backend (Docker). It supports online playback of Hongguo / Huangguo short dramas, OTP-based authentication for private mode, proxy bypass, and **download and merge on the phone or NAS**.

> This project originated from [MrSsg/HuangguoAPP-for-Andriod](https://github.com/MrSsg/HuangguoAPP-for-Andriod) (GPL-3.0), but has since evolved independently under the **Veyra** brand, with its own package name, backend image, and data directory. Content copyright belongs to the respective content sources; this project only provides the technical implementation. Do not use it for illegal purposes.

---

## Features

- **Multi-source playback**: Online playback of Hongguo / Huangguo short dramas. The backend address is entered by the user on the login / registration page, and **no private domain is built in**.
- **Account system**: Login / registration (the registration toggle is dynamically controlled in the WebUI). Registration requires an administrator dynamic code (OTP). Accounts are not tied to devices.
- **Private mode**: Requires a backend dynamic code (OTP), authenticated once and bound to the account. Administrator accounts enter directly without an OTP.
- **Proxy bypass**: A proxy port can be configured in settings (effective for Huangguo only). If the proxy is unreachable, traffic is automatically forwarded through the backend. Hongguo is unaffected.
- **Backend proxy**: The WebUI can configure the backend's outbound proxy (`http://ip:port`). When the backend fetches Huangguo resources, it goes through this proxy. proxy-test uses `google.com/generate_204` to check proxy connectivity.
- **Role permissions**: Regular users can only download to their phone. Administrators can download to NAS.
- **Download and merge**:
  - Phone: Concurrent download (10 streams), then local normalization and merge into a single file. If merging fails, the individual episodes are kept automatically, and merging can be retried or redone.
  - NAS: The backend uses ffmpeg to download, decrypt, and merge (avc3/hev1 + unified time base). The output is directly playable.
  - The phone-side merge engine is a **self-developed NDK-ported ffmpeg plus hand-written JNI** (the C layer handles decryption / normalization / concat). Its semantics align 1:1 with the backend downloader `server/downloader.js`.
- **WebUI admin console**: User list, role switching, user deletion, registration toggle, dynamic code display / reset, and backend proxy configuration. Access requires the administrator password (`ADMIN_PASSWORD`).

ihero3/dsh-image-video.body:
# 🎨 dsh-image-video — AI Text-to-Image / Text-to-Video plugin for DeepSeek Harness

**Registers two tools, `generate_image` and `generate_video`, for the DeepSeek Harness chat model. The model decides autonomously during conversation when to call them. Generated results are automatically downloaded to the local `outputs/` directory, and images are embedded and rendered through the attachment service. Create directly in the conversation without leaving the terminal.**

> The DSH ecosystem has plenty of tool plugins, but lacks a lightweight, install-and-use entry point for text-to-image and text-to-video. dsh-image-video fills that gap: two tools, four providers, zero external dependencies, hot-pluggable and ready to use.

## Core Features

- **Single image submission with idempotent recovery**: `imageTransport: auto` prefers async tasks. On submission timeout or 5xx, it only looks up the original task by `request_id`. By default it does not blindly resubmit, switch models, or generate candidates. When the async endpoint is not enabled, it safely falls back to a single synchronous submission.
- **Unified branded watermark post-processing**: Images have a configurable watermark applied in memory before being written to `outputsDir` and attachments. The desktop interactive stream displays the final watermarked image directly, and exposes the transport method, submission count, and post-processing metadata.
- **Two tools, natural-language triggering**: The model autonomously decides when to call `generate_image` / `generate_video` during conversation, with no manual commands needed.
- **Four providers with automatic routing by model family**: Threerouter (aggregator, default), Wanx (Alibaba Cloud Bailian), the MiniMax official platform, and Seedance2.5 (Volcano Engine). When a model is explicitly specified, a direct provider is selected automatically by family keyword. Threerouter always serves as the final fallback, and the fallback chain is recorded transparently in notes.
- **Async tasks do not block the conversation**: `TaskManager` uses `ctx.effect()` to manage the polling lifecycle. When the plugin is unloaded, queued tasks are cancelled automatically and timers are cleaned up, preventing memory leaks.
- **Inline image rendering**: Image bytes are persisted through the attachment service, and attachment references travel through the `presentationMeta` UI-only channel. The model sees only a text summary, so text-only models keep working.
- **Automatic reference image slimming**: Local reference images larger than 4MB are first scaled proportionally to a long edge of 2560, then converted to JPEG (q88) before submission. This avoids phone-original data URLs hitting gateway size limits or timeouts. Small images and remote URLs pass through unchanged.

# ZeroWeb

ZeroWeb is an experimental cross-platform browser written from scratch in Rust, supporting macOS, Linux, Windows, and Android. It delivers two things:

- **`ZeroWebView`**: a web rendering library that can be embedded in other applications
- **`ZeroBrowser`**: a complete browser application built on the same engine

DOM, CSS, layout, rendering, JavaScript bindings, networking, and security boundaries are all implemented in this repository, mainly relying on Rust components with permissive licenses.

This is also an AI-first engineering experiment: humans are responsible only for solution design, key decisions, and result verification, while nearly all code is written by AI. We want to see how far AI can push a complex system like a browser when architectural boundaries, tests, and acceptance criteria are clearly defined.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The project is in an experimental stage and **is not a browser for everyday use**. It is suitable for learning, research, and engineering exploration. For commercial or production use, please evaluate the risks related to features, security, compatibility, performance, and licensing yourself.

## Why this project

- **Embedding first**: In addition to the browser application, it provides a stable Rust `ZeroWebView` API for direct integration into other applications.
- **Clear licensing boundaries**: Mainline dependencies prefer permissive licenses such as MIT, Apache-2.0, and BSD, so core capabilities are not subject to copyleft constraints.
- **Full-stack Rust**: The page engine, host layer, and rendering infrastructure are kept within the Rust ecosystem wherever possible.

# lc-backend

## Service

1. A store owner (`owner`) registers a campaign (`campaign`). An administrator (`admin`) creates first-come, first-served coupon flyers from templates generated by an LLM, then pays for them to charge points.
2. Ad coupon feeds are served (`adserving`) to members (`member`). When a member views a coupon, points are charged (`billing`) based on that impression.
3. When a first-come, first-served coupon event starts, members receive a coupon (`coupon`). The store owner (`store`) scans the dynamic QR code in the member's coupon wallet to process coupon use.

## Tech Stack

* Language: Java 21 (`eclipse-temurin:21.0.9`)
* Build: Gradle 8.14.3 (wrapper)
* Framework: Spring Boot 4.0.5
* Database: MySQL 8.4, Valkey 9.0
* Data access: Spring Data JPA, QueryDSL, Flyway
* Authentication: Spring Security, OAuth2 Client, JJWT 0.12.7
* API docs: springdoc-openapi 3.0.3
* Resilience: resilience4j 2.4.0 (`spring-boot4`), 2.3.0 (`circuitbreaker`)
* Observability: Micrometer Prometheus, logstash-logback-encoder 8.0
* Testing: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, ArchUnit 1.4.1, JaCoCo 0.8.15
* Static analysis: SonarQube Gradle plugin 7.5.0.8588

## Structure

The project has three broad layers. Lower layers do not depend on upper layers.

| Layer | Role | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| 9 business domains | Own features and data | Reference only each other's `contract` |
| `auth`, `ops` | Lower-level submodules used by all domains | Do not depend on business domains |
| `global` | Exceptions, response format, distance calculation | Depend on nothing |

## Overview

This is a library for using Media over QUIC Transport (MOQT) in Rust. MOQT is a protocol for publishing and subscribing that runs on top of QUIC and WebTransport.

It can be used when implementing MOQT clients or servers.

## Features

- Implemented as Sans I/O, so it does not handle the network, timers, or threads
- Supports no_std and works with only `alloc`
- Dependencies are limited to `hashbrown` / `noflate` / `nojson` / `base64ct`

## Quick start

### Desktop app (recommended)

Download the latest `desktop-v*` release from [Releases](https://github.com/yann0917/voxbox/releases):

| Platform | File |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `VoxBox_*_aarch64.dmg` |

Install and open to use; no registration or login required. FFmpeg, which is needed for editing, the voice library, voice-clone synthesis, and similar features, is bundled, so it works out of the box.

> **First run on Windows**: In the SmartScreen popup, click "More info" → "Run anyway".

After opening, go to **Settings → Cloud Services** and enter the API key for each provider to use the corresponding cloud capabilities. Without any credentials, you can still use the Format Factory free channel and local inference (download engines and models under **Settings → Local Environment** to use them offline). The app checks for updates automatically on startup and upgrades in one click after you confirm.

### Web console (self-hosted)

Download the zip for your platform from the `v*` release on [Releases](https://github.com/yann0917/voxbox/releases). Unzipping yields a single executable file:

```bash
./voxbox serve --port 8081
# Open http://127.0.0.1:8081 in your browser
```

> On macOS, if you see "Apple could not verify", run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./voxbox` to remove the quarantine attribute.

Enter credentials on the Web settings page; they are fully consistent with the desktop version. You can also build from source: `make all` produces `bin/voxbox`.

Models, tasks and outputs, and the task database are stored by default in `~/.voxbox/data` (following the user's home directory).
